# @zakkster/lite-loglogn

Version: 0.2.0
License: MIT (c) Zahary Shinikchiev <shinikchiev@yahoo.com>
Runtime dependencies: none. ESM only. ASCII-only source. sideEffects: false.
Node: >= 18.

## What it is

A tree-shakeable, zero-GC family of sub-logarithmic bounded-integer
predecessor/successor data structures whose bound is proven by exact COUNTS. The
identity is the SPANNING framing: the family spans O(log_w U) to O(log log U)
over a bounded integer universe -- not a strict "O(log log U) only" package.
The FAMILY bound is O(log log U), in the universe size U (never the element
count n); StratifiedBitset itself is O(log_32 U), and XFastTrie is the first
strict O(log log U) member (queries only; its updates are O(w)). Every hot op
allocates zero bytes after construction.

It is the O(log log U) sibling of @zakkster/lite-o1 (the constant) and
@zakkster/lite-logn (the logarithm in n): lite-loglogn holds the double
logarithm in U. StratifiedBitset does NOT claim a log2(w) line; "log2(w) must
win" belongs to the strict O(log log U) members (XFastTrie shipped, others
planned), proven there by counts.

Keys are w-bit integers in [0, U), U <= 2^32 (bitwise ops are 32-bit); wider keys
are a labeled SegmentedU variant, never a silent BigInt hot path. The SPACE price
is a co-headline on every member, stated with the same prominence as the time bound.

Roster (one member per release, append-only). StratifiedBitset (0.2.0) and
XFastTrie (0.3.0) are shipped; YFastTrie and vEBTree are PLANNED:

- StratifiedBitset (0.2.0) -- array-embedded 32-ary bit pyramid. O(log_32 U)
  successor / predecessor; min / max read Lc words (Lc = levels <= 7);
  O(U/w) SPACE; 0 B/op on every hot method.
- XFastTrie (0.3.0) -- O(log log U) query via binary search over w pointer-free
  cuckoo LevelTables + a sorted leaf thread; O(w) UPDATE; O(n*w) SPACE,
  preallocated at a FIXED capacity.
- YFastTrie (0.4.0, planned) -- the O(n)-space fix over x-fast representatives;
  expected / amortized O(log log U).
- vEBTree (0.5.0, planned) -- flattened van Emde Boas; worst-case O(log log U); O(U) SPACE.

## Exports (from the single main file LogLogN.js)

- `VERSION` -- string. The package version; one of the three version sites
  (package.json / LogLogN.js VERSION const / this file's `Version:` header).
- `StratifiedBitset` -- class. An integer set over the fixed universe [0, U).
- `XFastTrie` -- class. An integer set over the fixed universe [0, U) with a
  fixed capacity; O(log log U) successor / predecessor, O(w) updates.

### StratifiedBitset

    import { StratifiedBitset } from '@zakkster/lite-loglogn';
    const s = new StratifiedBitset(1 << 20);
    s.add(5).add(70);                 // chainable, idempotent
    s.has(70);                        // true
    s.successor(5);                   // 70   (smallest key > 5)
    s.predecessor(70);                // 5    (largest key < 70)
    s.successor(70);                  // undefined (absent is undefined, never -1/null)
    for (let k = s.min(); k !== undefined; k = s.successor(k)) { /* walk */ }

Constructor: `new StratifiedBitset(universe)` -- universe an integer in
[1, 2^32] else RangeError `[lite-loglogn] universe must be an integer in
[1, 2^32]; got ...`. Fixed universe, no resize. Allocates one Uint32Array.

Getters (cold): `size`, `universe`, `levels` (= max(1, ceil(log2(U)/5)); 4 at
U = 2^16 and 2^20, 5 at 2^24, 6 at 2^28, 7 at 2^32), `byteLength` (4 x total
words of the one `_bits` Uint32Array).

Hot methods (0 B allocated):
- `has(x)` -> boolean
- `add(x)` -> this. Idempotent. Bad key -> RangeError `[lite-loglogn] key must be
  an integer in [0, U); got ...`, no state touched.
- `delete(x)` -> boolean (true if x was present)
- `successor(x)` -> number | undefined. STRICT: smallest key > x.
- `predecessor(x)` -> number | undefined. STRICT: largest key < x.
- `min()`, `max()` -> number | undefined (undefined when empty)

Cold: `clear()`; `dump()` -> { universe, size, words: Uint32Array[] } (ALLOCATES;
words[L] is a copy of level L, level 0 = key bits). No forEach, no iterator:
iterate with the successor walk.

Return conventions: absent = undefined (null is not zero, and not -1). -0 aliases
key 0. A bad key (not a number, non-integer, NaN, negative, >= U, null, string,
Symbol, BigInt, boxed Number) touches no word: has / delete -> false,
successor / predecessor -> undefined, add -> RangeError. For "at or after x" use
`s.has(x) ? x : s.successor(x)`.

Cost model (DETERMINISTIC; exact `_bits` word reads R / writes Wr, Lc = levels;
gated by test/Count.test.js through a counting Proxy over the shipped instance):
- has: R = 1
- add / delete when the key changes: R = Wr <= Lc (1 + the levels whose word
  changed emptiness); otherwise R = 1, Wr = 0
- successor / predecessor: R <= 2*Lc - 1 (a level-0 peel returns from the level-0
  word that holds x+1 / x-1 without touching level 1)
- min / max: R = Lc (R = 1 if empty)

Space (O(U/w); pinned in test/Space.test.js): U = 2^16 -> 8,460 B; 2^20 ->
135,300 B; 2^24 -> 2,164,804 B; 2^28 -> 34,636,836 B; 2^32 -> 554,189,332 B
(about 554 MB; the last two are formula values, never constructed in tests).

Boxing: hot methods allocate 0 bytes; a returned key >= 2^31 (>= 2^30 on a
pointer-compressed engine) may box as a HeapNumber when the call is not inlined.

### XFastTrie

    import { XFastTrie } from '@zakkster/lite-loglogn';
    const t = new XFastTrie(2 ** 32, 1024);   // universe, capacity (fixed)
    t.add(5).add(70);                         // chainable, idempotent
    t.successor(5);                           // 70   (STRICT, > 5)
    t.predecessor(70);                        // 5    (STRICT, < 70)
    t.successor(70);                          // undefined

Constructor: `new XFastTrie(universe, capacity)` -- universe an integer in
[2, 2^32], capacity an integer in [1, min(universe, 2^24)], else RangeError.
Allocates every column once; nothing is ever replaced except `_q` (nulled by a
poison, re-created by clear()). Getters (cold): `size`,
`universe`, `capacity`, `bits` (w = ceil(log2 U)), `byteLength`. Hot (0 B):
`has`, `add`, `delete`, `successor`, `predecessor`, `min`, `max` (same return
conventions as StratifiedBitset: absent = undefined, a bad key touches nothing,
-0 aliases 0, add of a bad key -> RangeError). Cold: `clear()` (restores the
default seeds, revives a poisoned instance), `dump()` -> { universe, capacity,
size, bits, keys: Uint32Array ascending, levels[L-1] = { capacity, prefix, min,
max } } (ALLOCATES).

Failure modes: add of a NEW key at size === capacity -> RangeError, no state
change. If 32 in-place reseed tries cannot place a key the add is rolled back
and throws RangeError; if the rollback itself fails the instance is POISONED:
every hot method throws TypeError on a valid key until clear().

Cost model (DETERMINISTIC; level-table TOUCHES counted through a Proxy over all
eight columns, test/XftCount.test.js; T = binary-search steps = log2(w) for
w = 2^j; m = shorter common prefix length of x with its thread neighbours):
- has: 1. successor / predecessor: 1 (x present), 1 + T (x absent). min / max: 0.
- add new key: 1 + T + (w - m). add present or full: 1.
- delete present: w - m. delete absent: 1. Any op with a bad key: 0.
- Rows are exact when no kick / reseed fires (add only).
- absent successor at w = 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 -> 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 touches; add into an
  empty trie (m = 0) -> 4, 7, 12, 21, 38 touches.

Caveats (stated plainly): FAST QUERY (1 + log2(w) touches when absent); O(w)
UPDATE (not O(log log U)); O(n*w) SPACE with FIXED capacity: byteLength =
13 TS + 12 (C+1) + 16 (w+1) + 16, TS = total level-table slots. Pinned
(DETERMINISTIC, test/XFastTrieSpace.test.js): (U, C) = (2^16, 1024) -> 225,580 B;
(2^20, 16384) -> 3,604,844 B; (2^32, 1) -> 3,896 B; (2^32, 65536) -> 31,457,836 B;
(2^32, 2^24) -> 4,563,403,308 B (worst case, formula only, about 4.6 GB). REPORTED
(node test/space-table.mjs, 2026-10-22, Node v26.8.2, deterministic bytes):
n = C = 1,000,000 at U = 2^20 -> 66,526,316 B vs StratifiedBitset 135,300 B
(491.7x); at U = 2^24 -> 175,578,284 B vs 2,164,804 B (81.1x); at U = 2^32 ->
393,682,220 B vs 554,189,332 B (0.71x). Dense universes favour StratifiedBitset;
XFastTrie pays off for a SPARSE set in a huge universe.
Hash-flood caveat: the cuckoo seeds are FIXED defaults, so adversarial keys can
force kick chains and reseeds (correctness holds, time suffers); see
decisions/0007-leveltable.md. Boxing: as StratifiedBitset (a returned key >= 2^31
may box when the call is not inlined).

## Gates and measurements (tiered)

- DETERMINISTIC (npm test = 342 tests, 0 fail, 2026-10-22, Node v26.8.2; also
  npm run verify = test + test:types + torture + test:perf): exact counts (words for
  StratifiedBitset, level-table touches for XFastTrie), seeded oracle fuzz,
  sibling oracles (lite-o1 BitSet / EliasFano, lite-logn Scapegoat + SortedArray;
  0 divergences), space pins, tier parity, bytecode-size gates, a parity pin of
  the StratifiedBitset region of the file against 0.2.0.
  `npm run torture`: T0 2,000,000 ops at U = 2^20 -> 0 B/op, gc major 0 / minor 0;
  XFastTrie lanes X0-X4 (QUIET verify run 2026-10-22, load1 1.32, baseline
  2.21, 12 cores, Node v26.8.2, 1 run): 2,000,000 ops at U = 2^20 and U = 2^30
  (C = 8192) -> 0 B/op, gc major 0 / minor 0, including kicks and reseeds
  (X2: 50,000 cycles natural and forced, abGrowth 0); X4's six must-fail controls flip (torture run 2026-10-23).
  `npm run test:perf`: PerfGate 14/14 (7 zero-alloc scenarios + 3 must-fail teeth +
  flag pin (2) + arrayBuffers attribution (1)) + XFastTriePerf 17/17 = 31/31 (same QUIET run).
- REPORTED (no CI for this package: statistical claims are REPORTED only; release-time,
  NOT in verify, 1 run each, exit 0 pass / 1 fail / 2 inconclusive): `npm run witness` (2026-10-22, Apple M4 Pro 12 cores, Node
  26.8.2, load1 3.66): member successor vs a local Uint32Array binary search at
  w = 28 won 15/0 at all nine n from 1e3 to 1e7 (member 11.74-17.84 ns/op;
  binary search 32.22 -> 197.78 ns/op). `npm run witness:tier` (the
  level-0 peel A/B; 2026-10-22T02:27:20Z, same host / Node, load1 4.79) returned EXIT 2 (inconclusive: a 1% A/A difference on identical
  code); the peel ships by maintainer waiver (dense-succ 11.5% and dense-pred
  16.5% faster, no scenario lost). The follow-up (ADR 0006 amendment): the
  XFastTrie A/B lane, `npm run witness:xft`, uses a 2% minimum-effect floor
  (test/helpers/abVerdict.mjs); tierVerdict is unchanged.
- REPORTED (docs only; same A8 run: 2026-10-22, Apple M4 Pro 12 cores, Node 26.8.2, load1 3.66, 1 run): the U-sweep fits better vs w (R^2 0.7293) than vs log2(w)
  (R^2 0.6589); no R^2 floor or slope band is gated. lite-o1 BitSet is faster where
  it applies (4.28-4.82 vs 4.87-7.61 ns/op at n = 4096, w = 16..24).

## Design bounds

- Zero runtime deps; node:test only; ASCII-only source.
- Single PascalCase main file LogLogN.js; sideEffects: false; tree-shakeable
  named exports, no barrel.
- Bounded integer universe, word-RAM model: keys are w-bit integers in [0, U),
  w <= 32. Fixed, preallocated capacity. Fail closed on every unverified state;
  `null` is not zero; an out-of-universe key fails closed.
- typeof-guard FIRST, before any coercion, at the door of every op (the recurring
  Symbol / BigInt / {valueOf} / boxed-Number footgun).
- Zero allocation on every steady-state hot path (0 B/op), proven by
  `node --expose-gc test/torture.mjs`.
- SPACE is a co-headline: every member states its footprint bound alongside its
  time bound.

## Cross-package boundaries

- @zakkster/lite-o1 -- the O(1) sibling. Any BOUNDED-INTEGER priority queue is
  O(1) and belongs there (Dial's bucket queue). Its BitSet: for U <= 2^25 and
  successor-only use lite-o1 BitSet (fixed 3 levels, O(1) in U); StratifiedBitset
  owns predecessor / max, U up to 2^32, labelled O(log_32 U), and returns undefined
  for absent (lite-o1 BitSet returns -1).
- @zakkster/lite-logn -- the O(log n) sibling. A general comparator ordered map is
  O(log n) and belongs there.
- @zakkster/lite-filter -- owns approximate / probabilistic membership;
  lite-loglogn owns exact ordered integer structures. No overlap; no use of it.
- @zakkster/lite-fastbit32 -- owns the clz32 / word-bit primitives; lite-loglogn
  cross-links its recipe, never a drifting reimplementation (decision D-05).
